## AWCDE Project -- Complete Analysis

### 1. What This Project Is About

**AWCDE** stands for **Adaptive Workload Characterization and Deployment Engine**. It is an open research project that transforms AI inference telemetry (from benchmarking tools like GuideLLM, NVIDIA AIPerf, etc.) into standardized, explainable **Workload Signatures** -- behavioral profiles that describe how an AI inference workload behaves.

The core hypothesis being validated:

> AI inference telemetry can be transformed into a standardized, explainable representation of workload behaviour that helps developers understand benchmark results and make better workload-aware decisions.

The project does NOT benchmark AI systems itself. It interprets results produced by existing benchmarking and observability tools. The primary artifact is the **Workload Signature**, which captures 8 behavioral dimensions (latency sensitivity, throughput orientation, memory intensity, burst behaviour, context length profile, concurrency profile, hardware affinity, modality). These signatures then feed into a rule-based KnowledgeBase to produce explainable infrastructure recommendations.

**Current Status**: The project is entirely in the **documentation/specification phase**. There is zero source code written. Phase 0 (Architecture & Specification) is complete. Phase 1 (Behavioural Model implementation) is in progress at the documentation level, but no code exists yet.
